Testimony of Rep. Benjamin Hymes
L.D. 1091, "An Act to Reinforce Free Speech at Town Meetings by Allowing Persons a
Minimum Amount of Time in Which to Speak"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government

March 31, 2025
Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government.
I am Representative Benjamin Hymes, proudly representing House District 38. I am here today to
present LD 1091, "An Act to Reinforce Free Speech at Town Meetings by Allowing Persons a
Minimum Amount of Time in Which to Speak" .

This bill as a straightforward First Amendment issue. While free speech and religious freedom
are frequently discussed, another critical part of the First Amendment is often overlooked: the
right to petition the government for a redress of grievances. This bill addresses a failure to uphold

that right for Maine citizens.

.

As elected officials, we understand the responsibilities of public service, including listening to those who disagree with us. It isn't always easy, but it is essential. Our role is to represent the people who elect us~--plain and simple. If we deny them the right to speak, we risk making policy in a vacuum. This is happening in Maine, and history shows that suppressing public input is how
tyrannical governments take hold.

This bill simply ensures that municipalities allow citizens a few minutes to exercise their First
Amendment right. It does not interfere with a municipality's ability to conduct orderly meetings or maintain decorum. The presiding official retains control over the meeting, ensuring discussions
remain respectful and productive.

Some have suggested setting a standard three-minute speaking limit, as we do here, or including
penalties for noncompliance. I leave these considerations to the committee's discretion.

Thank you for your time. I welcome any questions.

Benjamin C. Hymes
State Representative

District 38 Brooks, Jackson, Knox, Monroe, Swanville, Thorndike, Unity, Waldo & Frankfort (part)

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the State and Local Government
Committee, my name is Rebecca Lambert, and I am providing testimony in opposition to LD 1091 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) elected 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). For
reference, MMA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit member service organization and aims to help provide policy
solutions that work for all residents in Maine and the LPC guides the advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
Freedom of speech is a constitutional right that we all hold dear. When it comes to town meetings,
those with an open meeting format allow their residents an opportunity for floor discussions relating to a particular warrant article. During this time, residents can express their thoughts freely and are rarely limited in their length oftime to speak. -
However, just like when legislative committees are holding a public hearing on a hot topic, there are times when comments need to be limited in time to accommodate all who would like to address the board, in a fair and equitable manner. There are concerns among local leaders that requiring residents to have at least two minutes to speak at a town meeting could prevent town business from being conducted
effectively and could derail an ordinary business meeting.
Currently, towns have rules in place for the conduct of their town meetings and feel this bill is an unnecessary measure without a clear problem to point to. Thank you for your time and for considering the municipal perspective on this issue.
